paragraphs.text: The more we learn about whales, the better able we will be ①to protect them. This argument undoubtedly has merit. We would not be in a position today to argue for the rights of whales ②was it not for the scientific research that has been done. And if we could be certain ③that additional benign research would affect the benefit of the whales, who could oppose it? But history provides reason for skepticism. Sad though ④it is to say, science has been more often used against animals than for them. Sidney Holt has given one such example in which the results of benign research ⑤involving wolves are now being used against them. Who can have confidence that this will not be the case with the whales as well?
